Self-driving cars need to know where the road goes, in real time, with no prior map to lean on.

Self-driving cars need to know where the road goes, in real time, with no prior map to lean on. We’re building the perception-based world model stack that makes this possible. It takes raw multi-sensor input and produces a live, accurate 3D model of lanes, boundaries, crosswalks, intersection topology, and traffic control semantics. It also fuses perception, map, and localization data into a consistent model of the driving environment that the rest of the driving stack depends on. You will join a team of world-class software engineers improving these algorithms. This is a software engineering role: algorithms are only as good as the software that runs them, so we need an engineer who obsesses over quality, performance, and architecture, and who can turn algorithmic ideas into safe, fast, maintainable code for production vehicles on NVIDIA DRIVE Orin and Thor. Your code will meet ASIL-B/D requirements and ship across L2++, L3, and L4 programs. What you’ll be doing: Build and own core online world model and context fusion software that runs in the car, from architecture through implementation to deployment. Write production C++ for real-time embedded systems, with a focus on correctness, determinism, and maintainability. Design software architecture, interfaces, and data flows that promote code reuse and clean boundaries across vehicle programs, while meeting CPU, memory, and latency budgets. Profile complex pipelines, find bottlenecks, and deliver measurable improvements in CPU utilization, memory usage, and end-to-end latency, backed by reproducible measurements on Orin and Thor. Develop benchmarks and performance regression tests that track improvements and prevent regressions. Use GPU parallelism (CUDA) where it helps to accelerate compute-heavy mapping components. Implement and integrate algorithmic solutions from the mapping team into NVIDIA ’s AV stack, working closely with algorithm engineers to understand and refine them while preserving behavior, output quality, and correctness. Develop to automotive safety standards (ASIL-B/D): apply strong static analysis, follow safety-oriented coding guidelines, and achieve 100% line and branch coverage with rigorous unit and integration tests. Build software that is robust to the varied conditions and failure modes of vehicles operating around the world. Contribute to code reviews and uphold the team’s quality and safety expectations. What we need to see: PhD with 1+ year, MS with 3+ years, or BS with 5+ years of relevant experience in Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience. 5+ years of experience building robust, production-quality software 3+ years of professional modern C++ development, with a strong grasp of memory management, concurrency, and performance. Demonstrated ability to profile and optimize CPU utilization, memory consumption, and latency using profilers and benchmarks under representative workloads. Solid understanding of algorithms and data structures and their impact on performance. Experience designing software architecture and APIs for large, long-lived codebases. A quality-first, systematic approach to debugging and optimization: comfort with static analysis, unit testing, and high-coverage test strategies. Overview Lynker is seeking a highly skilled Software Engineer to support the NOAA/NWS Office of Modeling and Development by managing, developing, and optimizing the meteorological data decoder systems. This role focuses on the critical pipeline that converts diverse, native-format meteorological observations into standardized formats required for downstream numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems. Responsibilities Duties of the Scientific Software Engineer will include the following: Technical Operations & R&D Develop, maintain, and optimize C and Fortran programs used to decode raw meteorological bulletins. Translate non-standard native data formats into BUFR and JEDI IODA netcdf by engineering specialized decoder logic Ensure uninterrupted, efficient data flow by managing input and output streams for ingest data queues, descriptor lists, and temporary BUFR message storage. Systems & Data Integration Monitor and troubleshoot operational data ingestion across major meteorological data servers, including LDM, DBNet, GTS, and WIS2. Ensure decoded data tanks are optimized for rapid assimilation into the NCEP NWP system, supporting the generation of thousands of daily weather products. Manage and maintain the software repositories pertaining to legacy and operational decoder processing. Coordination & Reporting Liaise with upstream data originators and downstream NCO Operations users to seamlessly integrate new observational data types into the BUFR pipeline. Report on software task progress, system performance metrics, and project risks to the Lead Scientist and Federal oversight managers. Participate in the Modernization of Observation Infrastructure project (GEODE) to transition legacy decoder frameworks to modern architectures. Qualifications The Scientist Software Engineer selected for this role should meet the following qualifications: Advanced skills and knowledge of Fortran and C programming languages specifically tailored for data parsing and processing. Deep understanding of BUFR (Binary Universal Form for the Representation of meteorological data), including table-driven descriptors and binary extraction logic. Experience working in a UNIX/Linux environment with advanced shell scripting languages. Demonstrated knowledge of meteorological data servers and distribution networks (LDM, DBNet, GTS, WIS2). Skills and knowledge of High-Performance Computing (HPC) file systems and job schedulers (e.g., WCOSS environment, MPI, Slurm, LSF). Knowledge of modern software development practices and version control software, particularly Git/GitHub/Gitflow. Ability to perform complex, mission-critical debugging in a fast-paced, operational environment. Additional desirable experiences and skills include: Knowledge of global Data Assimilation (DA) systems and observation networks. Experience transitioning legacy meteorological codebases into Cloud environments. Background in atmospheric physics or earth system modeling. About Lynker Lynker is a growing, employee owned business, specializing in professional, scientific and technical services. Our continually expanding team combines scientific expertise with mature, results-driven processes and tools to achieve technically sound, cost effective solutions in hydrology/water sciences, geospatial analysis, information technology, resource management, conservation, and management and business process improvement. In 2026, most estimates put rates at $15–25 an hour for juniors, $25–45 for mid-level, $35–65 for seniors and $50–80 for leads, about $2,400–$12,800 a month full-time. The rate is the easy part. What decides success is interviewing the actual engineers, running a paid trial sprint and getting IP ownership in writing.

Our guide to custom web application development cost compared developer rates by region. The next questions are practical ones. Dedicated team, freelancer or fixed-price project? What should the contract say? How do you know a team is good before you commit?

We're a Delhi studio, so we have an obvious interest in the answer. We've also spent 18+ years and 3,000+ projects on these engagements, and we've seen what makes them work and what makes them fail. This guide covers both, including when you shouldn't hire in India at all.

Why companies hire dedicated web developers from India

Three reasons come up again and again.

Talent depth. India's tech industry directly employs about 5.95 million people, according to Nasscom's 2026 Strategic Review. GitHub's Octoverse 2025 counted 21.9 million Indian developers on the platform, with more than 5.2 million joining in 2025 alone, and projects India will have the world's largest developer community by 2030.

Cost. A full-time Indian developer costs well under a comparable US hire. The realistic saving is smaller than the "70%" in vendor ads (we do the maths below), but it still buys more engineering, more testing or a longer runway.

Speed. Most published estimates put the time to fill a senior engineering role in the US or UK at two to four months, before notice periods. A good dedicated team provider already has vetted engineers and can usually start within days or weeks.

Dedicated team vs fixed-price project vs freelancer vs in-house

"Hiring Indian developers" can mean four very different arrangements. Choose the model first, then the vendor.

Freelancer

Best for small, well-defined tasks: a landing page, a plugin, a bug fix. Fast to start and cheap per hour. The risks are continuity (one person, no holiday cover), no built-in code review and IP terms that depend entirely on what you get them to sign.

Fixed-price project
